radar: The pointed nose of the jet cut open: the round flat weather-radar dish on its mount behind the radome, equipment racks behind it, the cockpit windows above and the jet bridge at the lower right.
cockpit: The flight deck at the front of the upper deck: two pilots in white shirts at the controls with instrument screens and an overhead panel, the cockpit windows to the left, the start of the upper-deck cabin to the right, electronics racks below.
avionics: The nose section below the flight deck: shelves of grey electronics boxes and wiring in the electronics bay, the radar dish at the left, first class seats above, the nose belly and jet bridge below.
first-class: The first class cabin in the nose on the main deck: wide blue seats with passengers and a flight attendant, the front door, electronics racks below, the flight deck above.
upper-deck: The upper deck under the hump: a cabin of seats with passengers and windows, and the staircase leading down to the main deck with people on it, with the cockpit at the left.
jet-bridge: The jet bridge: a grey telescoping tunnel on a support leg, connected to the front main-deck door, with the nose landing gear and pushback tug below and the nose cabins above.
cabin: The long economy cabin on the main deck: many rows of blue seats with seated passengers, two aisles, overhead bins, windows and flight attendants, with the cargo hold containers below.
fuselage: The smooth white upper body panels of the airliner above the main passenger cabin, with the structural frames and stringers visible where panels are left off, the overhead luggage bins below, and the far wing with its two engines rising behind.
cargo: The lower-deck cargo hold: rows of grey metal luggage containers and suitcases on a roller floor, baggage handlers in hi-vis vests, the conveyor belt loader at the forward cargo door, and the top of the near wing below.
wing: The near left wing seen from above, top skin cut away to show spars, ribs and fuel tank cells, flaps along the trailing edge, ending in an upturned winglet with a blue edge, with the engines below it.
flaps: The trailing edge of the near wing: flap panels and their canoe-shaped track fairings along the edge, the open wing structure next to it, and the ground beyond.
engine: The inboard engine under the near wing with its cowling cut away: big front fan with many curved blades, compressor stages, orange combustion section, turbine and exhaust cone, hanging on its pylon; the outboard engine to the right, a fueller and the fuel hose below.
landing-gear: The main landing gear: several four-wheel bogies with shock struts and black tyres standing on the apron under the wing root, with the wing above.
galley: The rear galley on the main deck: metal meal trolleys, ovens and cabinets, flight attendants and a caterer, the rear passenger door at the right with the catering truck platform outside, the cabin seats at the left.
bulkhead: The rear of the cabin: the domed rear pressure bulkhead shown as curved rings of frames, the rear passenger door with the catering truck platform below it, and the tail structure behind.
tail: The tall tail fin with its skin cut away to show spars and ribs, the rudder along the back edge with a blue stripe, the horizontal stabilizer below, and the tail cone.
apu: The tail cone cut open: the small auxiliary power unit engine with pipes inside, a bright orange flight recorder box, the pointed exhaust at the tip, and the horizontal stabilizer just below.
recorder: Inside the cut-open tail cone: a bright orange flight recorder box sitting among pipes and the small APU engine, with the horizontal stabilizer below.
pushback: The low white pushback tug with yellow and black chevrons connected to the two-wheel nose landing gear, a ground crew member in a hi-vis vest, and the jet bridge leg.
baggage: The baggage team: a small baggage tug pulling trolleys of colorful suitcases, the conveyor belt loader carrying bags up into the forward cargo door, handlers in hi-vis vests and orange cones.
fuel-truck: The white fuel tanker truck with a blue stripe under the near wing, its black hose rising to the wing, a fueller in a hi-vis vest, the engines above.
catering: The catering high-loader truck: a white box raised on black scissor arms beside the rear door, platforms with caterers in hi-vis vests, the truck cab and wheels below.
